newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bonds marked time in dreary Monday trade characterised only by a lack of interest and direction, dealers said.
At the finish, the key R150 stock was pegged at a 15.33 percent yield compared with Friday's 15.36 percent finish.
The market initially perked up on offshore buying in the wake of reserves data on Friday which was in line with economists' expectations.
The Reserve Bank's holdings of gold and foreign exchange eased 292.06 million rand in August to 10.078 billion rand from July's 10.37 billion rand.
Dealers said hopes that July producer inflation would better market expectations also lured some buyers into the market, which took the R150 to an intraday low of 15.295 percent.

But the PPI data matched a consensus forecast of a 0.8 percent month-on-month rise and a 6.6 percent year-on-year rise and the R150 touched its morning's worst level of 15.34 percent shortly after the data's 0900 GMT release.
In the afternoon session, yields inched higher to a day's worst of 15.365 percent amid small-scale jobber activity, while institutions held to the sidelines.
"The institutions are not moving into the market at these levels because they don't see value here," a dealer said.
"On the whole the market has been a non-event today," he added.
Dealers said that in its search for fresh direction, the bond market would look to the rand.
But any hopes that the currency would oblige immediately were shot down after the rand patrolled a narrow 4.4900 to 4.5000 range all day.
A currency trader said the rand had been helped at the opening by an overspill of New York dollar selling from Friday as well as exporter selling.
Activity was muted for much of the day until more dollars were again injected by New York players, which helped the currency finish near it's best level of the day.
It was last quoted at 4.4930/4980 from 4.5040/5070 on Friday.
"There is some talk that the rand might go to 4.45 this week," a dealer said, citing the breach on the downside of the 4.5025 level.
"But I think that is unlikely because there will be a lot of orders left around the 4.47 level to buy dollars."
Against the crosses, it was last quoted at 7.0041/0164 on sterling from 7.0376/0499 on Friday and at 0.3315/3320 marks from 0.3300/3304 marks previously.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 136.898 million rand of South African bonds on Friday after buying 34.05 million rand on Thursday. Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 4.46 billion rand from 39.17 billion rand on Thursday, which is a settlement date. On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.90 and 16.10 percent, while 90-day BAs were also unmoved at between 15.35 to 15.50 percent.
The Reserve Bank put the money market shortage at 8.273 billion rand on Saturday from 8.219 billion rand on Friday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
